title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, code quality, infrastructure, model serving, observability, and performance. It also catalogs key Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) relevant to these areas. The goal is to provide a single source-of-truth for engineers and product teams to design, review, and operate services that meet our reliability, security, and cost targets.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing and internal services that touch inference, routing, storage of model artifacts, or telemetry ingestion.
- Includes hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes where behavior or constraints differ, call-outs are provided.

Guiding Principles

1. Predictable economics: prefer designs that make latency/cost trade-offs explicit and measurable.
2. Observable by default: services must emit structured traces, metrics, and logs for SLOs and incident triage.
3. Minimal blast radius: use isolation (namespaces, VPCs, dedicated pools) for customer-sensitive paths.
4. Reproducible infra: all infra changes must be in Terraform/IaC and reviewed.
5. API and contract stability: semantic versioning for public APIs, compatibility tests for internal contracts.

Ownership and Review Process

- Ownership: the platform architecture working group owns these standards. Individual service owners are responsible for compliance.
- Review: proposals that affect multiple standards must open an ADR and a PR against this doc with the relevant checklist completed.

API Standards

Overview
- Use REST or gRPC depending on latency/streaming requirements. Public (customer) APIs should be REST/JSON with stable endpoints. Internal high-throughput paths (model RPC between runtime services) may use gRPC with proto contracts.

Design rules
- Versioning: API paths must include a major version (e.g., /v1/generate). Backwards-compatible changes increment minor; breaking changes increment major.
- Idempotency: non-idempotent mutation endpoints must accept an idempotency key header (X-Idempotency-Key).
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Use limit + cursor pattern.
- Error model: consistent error envelope {code,int,error_message,string,details,array}. Map errors to HTTP status codes and structured error codes (e.g., INFER-001: model-unavailable).
- Rate limits & quotas: service-level default quotas; per-customer overrides stored in RBAC/Quota service. Document rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset).

Security
- All public APIs require TLS 1.2+ and cert pinning for critical client SDKs.
- Authentication: JWT for service-to-service; OAuth2/Bearer tokens for external customers.
- Input validation: maximum payload sizes and strict schema validation on all public endpoints to avoid resource exhaustion and model prompt injection.

Examples
- Generation request: POST /v1/generate {"model":"redwood-compat-1","prompt":"..."}
- Streaming: use server-sent events or chunked gRPC streams for token-level streaming.

Coding Standards

General rules
- Languages: primary backend languages are Go (services), Python (ML/eval pipelines), and TypeScript (console/frontend).
- Formatting & linting: CI enforces gofmt/golangci-lint, black/flake8 for Python, and eslint/prettier for TS.
- Tests: every PR must include unit tests; services must have >80% coverage for critical modules; integration tests for cross-service contracts.
- Dependency management: use language-specific package lock files; approve dependency upgrades through Dependabot + security review.

Code review checklist
1. API/contract changes documented with migration strategy.
2. Performance-sensitive code has benchmarks or complexity analysis.
3. Error paths and telemetry added.
4. Secrets & credentials are not checked in.
5. Rollback plan included for risky changes.

Infra Standards

Provisioning and IaC
- Terraform is the canonical IaC tool for cloud resources. All stateful resources must be tagged with service, owner, and cost-center tags.
- Changes to networking, IAM, or persistent storage require a security review and cross-team signoff.

Networking & Security
- VPC design: multi-AZ private subnets for runtime services; NAT gateways only where necessary.
- Least privilege: IAM roles scoped to required actions; use short-lived credentials where possible.
- KMS/HSM: all customer sensitive keys and encryption must be integrated with the configured KMS.

Capacity & GPU Fleet
- Autoscaling: use target-based autoscaling for replica counts and a separate horizontal autoscaler for GPU-backed worker pools.
- Reservation: Dedicated customers use pinned capacity pools; enforce soft-limits at admission to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Cost controls: periodic reclamation job for idle GPU sessions and TTLs for ephemeral test clusters.

Model-Serving Standards

Runtime contracts
- Model artifacts: models must include a manifest.json with metadata (model_name, version, tokenization, quantization_profile, input_schema).
- API compatibility: the serving runtime must support a stable InferenceAPI proto with fields: request_id, model_id, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, stop_tokens.
- KV cache semantics: KV cache entries are per-customer and per-model-version and must be invalidated on model version rollback.

Quantization & Profiles
- Quantization profiles are recommended per-model and stored alongside artifacts. Profiles must be labeled with a quality delta (e.g., Q-0.5% to indicate 0.5% quality loss) and validated with automated evals.

Rollouts and Canarying
- Canary rules: default 2% traffic canary for new model versions, 5-10% for higher-risk changes. Canary monitors: latency P50/P95, error rate, and quality regression on a representative prompt set.
- Automatic rollback: triggers configured to rollback on threshold breaches (see Performance SLOs below).

Observability Standards

Metrics & SLOs
- Metric naming: use dot-separated metric names with service and domain: inference.request.count, inference.latency.p95_ms. All metrics must include service and model labels.
- Tracing: distributed tracing required for request paths that cross services. Trace sampling: 100% for canaries and 1% baseline for production.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with fields {ts, service, level, request_id, span_id, model_id, customer_id?}. PII must be redacted before logging.
- SLOs: define service SLOs in owner runbooks. Platform default SLOs: availability 99.95% (monthly), P95 latency for /v1/generate <= 350ms for hosted small-models tier, error rate <= 0.05%.

Alerting and Runbooks
- Alerts must map to runbooks with specific triage steps, owners, and escalation policies.
- Noise reduction: use composite alerts and rate-based triggers to avoid pager fatigue.

Performance Standards

Benchmarking and Targets
- Benchmarks: every model and runtime change must run against the canonical benchmarking suite (see benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Track throughput (tokens/s), latency percentiles (P50/P90/P95/P99), memory, and GPU utilization.
- Target guidelines (hosted): small models target P95 < 350ms, medium models < 600ms, large models < 1200ms for single-turn generation with 128 tokens.
- Efficiency metrics: cost-per-token and tokens-per-GPU-hour should be reported to finance for capacity planning.

Optimization practices
- Batching: use adaptive batching with max batching window 50ms; prefer latency-first policies for low-latency endpoints.
- Cache: enable prefix/KV caching for chat and reranking workloads with TTLs tuned per workload.
- Kernel selection: runtime should automatically pick optimized kernels per device; annotate experiments with kernel versions used.

Decision Records (ADRs)

- ADR-2025-01: Standardize on proto-based internal model RPCs (author: Daniel Ruiz, status: accepted, date: 2025-02-10). Rationale: gRPC/proto enables strong typing, smaller payloads, and easier evolution across polyglot runtimes. Consequence: added CI step to generate protos and compatibility checks.

- ADR-2025-07: API Versioning Policy (author: Mei Chen, status: accepted, date: 2025-07-02). Rationale: minimize customer disruptions while allowing iterative improvements. Consequence: include major version in path and maintain compatibility matrix.

- ADR-2026-01: Default Canary Size & Auto-Rollback (author: Aisha Patel, status: in_review, date: 2026-01-20). Proposal: default 2% canary, automated rollback on >3x baseline error rate or >=20% P95 latency regression.

How to add an ADR

1. Fork the docs repo and add an ADR markdown under /adrs with the template (title, status, context, decision, consequences, date, authors).
2. Open a PR and tag architecture working group.
3. After acceptance, add an entry to this page and update related checklists.

Compliance and Enforcement

- CI gates: checks for lint, tests, schema validation, and contract tests must pass before merge.
- Architecture reviews: changes to infra, model-serving, public APIs, or cost > $X/month require a design review and documented ADR if they alter standards.

Appendix: Example Audit Checklist for Service Owners

- API: versioning, idempotency, documented quotas.
- Security: TLS, auth, input validation, KMS integration.
- Observability: metrics emitted, traces propagated, logs structured and PII-redacted.
- Performance: benchmark results and cost estimate.
- Infra: Terraform changes in review, network and IAM impacts documented.
